title: Data jurisdiction safeguards and region-lock constraints for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customers running Private/VPC and on-prem Redwood must be able to assert that data never leaves an approved legal jurisdiction (country/region), that retention and deletion policies are enforced at the data plane, and that auditors can be provided cryptographically verifiable evidence that residency and retention controls were applied. This ticket implements a combined control plane + data plane mechanism to enforce region lock (no cross-jurisdiction failover by default), retention TTL enforcement, and automated evidence/reporting generation for audits.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane exposes a 'region_lock' flag per deployment that can be set to COUNTRY or REGION level

Data plane enforces traffic routing and storage placement so that reads/writes for a region-locked deployment stay within allowed AZs/regions; no automatic cross-country failover without explicit override
Retention settings configurable per-deployment with immutable deletion proofs: when TTL expires, system emits signed deletion manifest and retention-proof artifact stored in customer audit bucket

Automated nightly evidence report generated for each private deployment that includes: current residency policy, list of storage endpoints used in last 30 days, key rotation timestamps, and signed audit events (ED25519/KMS), and is retained according to customer-specified evidence retention policy
Audit evidence can be exported as a single signed archive; legal team can validate signatures using public key provided in Confluence
E2E tests (simulated cross-region outage) demonstrate that failover respect 'region_lock' resulting in either degraded mode or queued requests rather than cross-jurisdiction routing
Policy changes are visible in Console and via API; change events are recorded in the customer's audit log stream
tasks: Design policy spec for region_lock semantics and ties to deployment metadata
Implement control-plane API: set/get region_lock and retention policy
Add enforcement hooks in serving runtime to refuse cross-region route when region_lock is active
Extend storage placement logic to prefer same-country replicas and tag objects with jurisdiction metadata
Build evidence generator: signed manifests, event bundler, and nightly report job
Integrate evidence store with customer-managed KMS option (wrap signatures with customer key when configured)
Console and API surface updates for viewing/downloading evidence and configuring residence/retention
Create E2E test harness and chaos scenario for failover behavior
design_notes: We avoid automatic cross-country failover by default; allow explicit tenant-level opt-in for emergency cross-region failover that creates immutable audit events
Evidence artifacts are JSONL bundles signed by a cluster signing key; when a customer provides a KMS key we additionally wrap the cluster signature with a customer-wrapped signature token
Use object metadata tags (x-redwood-jurisdiction) on storage blobs to make placement auditable without scanning content
Retention enforcement uses tombstones + asynchronous shredder to provide deletion proofs: shredder emits signed 'shred event' when object removed and records object_digest + deletion_timestamp
For on-prem/private deployments we provide a local evidence collector that can push a daily signed bundle to a customer-specified S3-compatible endpoint or to an internal vault
infra_changes: Add policy-check middleware in gateway to reject routes crossing jurisdiction boundary
Storage placement enhancement: region-aware bucketing and mandatory tagging
Audit event pipeline: persistent event queue + signer service + evidence archival job
Metrics and alerts for residency violations (should be zero) and blocked cross-region failover attempts
test_plan: Unit tests for policy enforcement functions
Integration tests: simulate deployment in eu-west and attempt routed request to us-east; expect rejection when region_lock set
E2E: orchestrate region failover simulation (instance termination) and validate that requests are queued, returned error, or require manual override depending on config
Fuzz tests for evidence generator to ensure signed archives validate against public key
Pen test focused on evidence endpoint to ensure signatures cannot be replayed or forged
rollout_plan: Feature-gated rollout in private control plane; opt-in customers invited for alpha
Start with read-only monitoring mode for 2 weeks (control plane logs violations but does not block)
Enable enforcement for alpha cohort (private + Dedicated customers) after legal sign-off
Gradual rollout to all Private installs with a 30-day notice and migration tooling
Provide manual override path for emergency cross-jurisdiction failover; requires 2 engineer approvals and emits high-fidelity evidence
